from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        lecture_lines = [
            "Legend says monks move sixty-four disks between three pillars.",
            "Only one disk moves at a time.",
            "Larger disks cannot sit on smaller ones."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Legend and the Rules", lecture_lines)

        # Colors from storyboard
        PILLAR_COLOR = "#808080"
        RED_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        BLUE_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        GLOW_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Legend says monks move sixty-four disks between three pillars.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(PILLAR_COLOR))
        
        # Create 3 pillars
        # Height 3.5 roughly covers rows C to F
        p1 = Rectangle(height=3.5, width=0.2, fill_color=PILLAR_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        p2 = Rectangle(height=3.5, width=0.2, fill_color=PILLAR_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        p3 = Rectangle(height=3.5, width=0.2, fill_color=PILLAR_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.place_in_area(p1, "C2", "F2")
        self.place_in_area(p2, "C4", "F4")
        self.place_in_area(p3, "C6", "F6")
        
        # Create Disks as specified
        # Heights are set to 0.6 to look good in 1.0 unit grid cells
        d_blue = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=1.6, fill_color=BLUE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        d_green = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=1.1, fill_color=GREEN_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        d_red = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=0.6, width=0.6, fill_color=RED_COLOR, fill_opacity=1, stroke_color=WHITE, stroke_width=1)
        
        # Initial stack on Pillar 1
        self.place_at_grid(d_blue, "F2")
        self.place_at_grid(d_green, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(d_red, "D2")
        
        self.play(
            Create(VGroup(p1, p2, p3)),
            FadeIn(VGroup(d_blue, d_green, d_red), shift=UP*0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Only one disk moves at a time.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Move smallest Red disk from P1 (D2) to P2 (F4)
        # Using path_arc to create a "jump" effect
        self.play(
            d_red.animate.move_to(self.grid["F4"]),
            path_arc=-PI/2,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Larger disks cannot sit on smaller ones.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Try to move largest Blue disk onto Red disk (on P2)
        # Target is E4 (cell above Red disk which is at F4)
        start_pos_blue = d_blue.get_center()
        invalid_target = self.grid["E4"]
        
        self.play(
            d_blue.animate.move_to(invalid_target),
            path_arc=-PI/3,
            run_time=1.2
        )
        
        # Show red "X" to indicate illegal move
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT),
            Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT)
        ).set_color(RED_COLOR).scale(0.4).move_to(invalid_target + UP*0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(cross))
        self.play(Flash(cross, color=RED_COLOR, line_length=0.2, flash_radius=0.3))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Illegal move: return Blue disk to start
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cross),
            d_blue.animate.move_to(start_pos_blue),
            path_arc=PI/3,
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Final setup highlight with glow
        glow = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(p1, p2, p3, d_blue, d_green, d_red), color=GLOW_COLOR, buff=0.4, stroke_width=2)
        self.play(Create(glow))
        self.play(glow.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.3))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Final cleanup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(glow),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the scene with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Binary Counter", [
            "Binary counting uses only zeros and ones.",
            "In three bits, we count from zero to seven.",
            "Notice how each bit toggles at a specific frequency."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color match: #ADD8E6 (Light Blue) for the initial binary text
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        
        binary_val_text = Text("000", font_size=60, color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_in_area(binary_val_text, "C2", "D5")
        
        self.play(Write(binary_val_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color match: #555555 (Dark Gray) for the initial state of the circles
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#555555")
        )
        
        # Create 3 circles representing the bits
        circles = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=0.35, fill_opacity=1, color="#555555", stroke_width=2) 
            for _ in range(3)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(circles, "C2", "D5")
        
        # Replace the digits with the circles
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(binary_val_text, circles)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color match: #FFFF00 (Bright Yellow) for the toggling bits
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        
        # Target position for circles (shifting down)
        circles_target_pos = self.grid["D3"] + RIGHT * 0.9 # Visual centering hack within grid
        
        # Reposition circles to make room for text above
        self.play(
            circles.animate.move_to(circles_target_pos)
        )
        
        # Display the corresponding binary string above the circles
        counter_text = Text("000", font_size=48, color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_in_area(counter_text, "B2", "C5")
        self.play(FadeIn(counter_text))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Increment from 001 (1) to 111 (7)
        for i in range(1, 8):
            bin_str = bin(i)[2:].zfill(3)
            
            # Prepare new text and bit colors
            new_text_mob = Text(bin_str, font_size=48, color="#ADD8E6")
            new_text_mob.move_to(counter_text.get_center())
            
            anims = [Transform(counter_text, new_text_mob)]
            
            for bit_idx, char in enumerate(bin_str):
                # The circles index is 0, 1, 2 for bits from left to right
                target_color = "#FFFF00" if char == '1' else "#555555"
                anims.append(circles[bit_idx].animate.set_color(target_color))
            
            self.play(*anims, run_time=0.6)
            self.wait(0.4)
            
        self.wait(3)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            "Every disk corresponds to a specific binary bit.",
            "Disk one is the rightmost, least significant bit.",
            "Moving n disks requires two to the n minus one moves.",
            "The current move number identifies which disk to move.",
            "Watch as move numbers map to specific disks."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mapping: Disks as Bits", lecture_lines)
        
        # Color definitions from storyboard
        DISK_COLOR = "#90EE90"  # Light Green
        BIT_COLOR = "#00FFFF"   # Cyan
        FORMULA_COLOR = "#FFFFFF" # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Every disk corresponds to a specific binary bit."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Visual representations of disks
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, height=0.3, width=0.8, color=DISK_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, height=0.3, width=1.1, color=DISK_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.05, height=0.3, width=1.4, color=DISK_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        # Labels for disks
        l1 = Text("Disk 1", font_size=18, color=DISK_COLOR)
        l2 = Text("Disk 2", font_size=18, color=DISK_COLOR)
        l3 = Text("Disk 3", font_size=18, color=DISK_COLOR)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(l1, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(l2, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(disk3, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(l3, "D3")
        
        self.play(
            Create(disk1), Write(l1),
            Create(disk2), Write(l2),
            Create(disk3), Write(l3),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Disk one is the rightmost, least significant bit."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BIT_COLOR)
        
        # Mapping labels as requested: "Disk X -> Bit Y"
        m1 = Text("Disk 1 -> Bit 0", font_size=18, color=BIT_COLOR)
        m2 = Text("Disk 2 -> Bit 1", font_size=18, color=BIT_COLOR)
        m3 = Text("Disk 3 -> Bit 2", font_size=18, color=BIT_COLOR)
        
        self.place_at_grid(m1, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(m2, "C5")
        self.place_at_grid(m3, "D5")
        
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=l1.get_right(), end=m1.get_left(), color=BIT_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=l2.get_right(), end=m2.get_left(), color=BIT_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        arrow3 = Arrow(start=l3.get_right(), end=m3.get_left(), color=BIT_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(arrow1), Write(m1))
        self.play(Create(arrow2), Write(m2), Create(arrow3), Write(m3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Moving n disks requires two to the n minus one moves."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(FORMULA_COLOR)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\text{Total Moves} = 2^n - 1", color=FORMULA_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "The current move number identifies which disk to move."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(DISK_COLOR)
        
        binary_info_text = Text("Move Number in Binary:", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        binary_info_math = MathTex(r"\dots b_2 b_1 b_0", color=BIT_COLOR)
        binary_info = VGroup(binary_info_text, binary_info_math).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(binary_info, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_info))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Watch as move numbers map to specific disks."
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Sequence of highlights to emphasize the mapping
        self.play(
            Indicate(disk1, color=BIT_COLOR),
            Indicate(m1, color=WHITE),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(disk2, color=BIT_COLOR),
            Indicate(m2, color=WHITE),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(disk3, color=BIT_COLOR),
            Indicate(m3, color=WHITE),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "To find the disk, write the move number in binary.",
            "Find the position of the rightmost digit one.",
            "Position one means move the smallest disk.",
            "Position two means move the second smallest disk.",
            "This pattern holds for every move in the puzzle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Rule of the Rightmost Set Bit", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the decimal number '4' and its binary equivalent '100'
        decimal_4 = Text("4", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        arrow_to_bin = MathTex("\\rightarrow", color=WHITE)
        binary_4 = MathTex("1", "0", "0", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        
        # Placing at grid locations
        self.place_at_grid(decimal_4, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow_to_bin, "B4", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_4, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(decimal_4), Write(arrow_to_bin), Write(binary_4))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Underline the '1' in '100' with a gold color (#FFD700) 
        # and display the text 'Rightmost 1 at position 3' below it.
        # binary_4[0] is the digit '1' in '100'
        underline = Underline(binary_4[0], color="#FFD700", buff=0.1)
        pos_label = Text("Rightmost 1\nat position 3", font_size=20, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(pos_label, "C5", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(underline))
        self.play(FadeIn(pos_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Position one means move the smallest disk.
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.5, height=0.2, color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        disk1_label = Text("Disk 1", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(disk1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        disk1_group = VGroup(disk1, disk1_label)
        self.place_at_grid(disk1_group, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(disk1_group))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Position two means move the second smallest disk.
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.8, height=0.2, color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        disk2_label = Text("Disk 2", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(disk2, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        disk2_group = VGroup(disk2, disk2_label)
        self.place_at_grid(disk2_group, "E4", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(disk2_group))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This pattern holds for every move... 
        # Show an arrow pointing from the gold '1' to a graphic of 'Disk 3'
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.1, height=0.2, color="#1E90FF", fill_opacity=0.8)
        disk3_label = Text("Disk 3", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(disk3, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        disk3_group = VGroup(disk3, disk3_label)
        self.place_at_grid(disk3_group, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Arrow from the underlined '1' to Disk 3
        rule_arrow = Arrow(
            start=underline.get_bottom(),
            end=disk3_group.get_top(),
            color="#FFD700",
            stroke_width=3,
            buff=0.1
        )

        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(disk3_group))
        self.play(Create(rule_arrow))
        self.wait(2)

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        title_str = "Conclusion: Mathematical Elegance"
        lines = [
            "Binary logic transforms a complex puzzle into simple counting.",
            "Computers use this efficiency to solve recursive problems.",
            "The Tower of Hanoi hides a binary heartbeat."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)

        # Colors for matching lecture lines with animation elements
        bridge_color = "#B0C4DE"
        tower_highlight = "#FFA500"
        final_white = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Set matching color for line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color(bridge_color)
        
        # Create 'Binary Bridge' visual
        # Top and bottom horizontal lines
        top_line = Line(start=self.grid["B1"], end=self.grid["B6"], color=bridge_color, stroke_width=4)
        bottom_line = Line(start=self.grid["D1"], end=self.grid["D6"], color=bridge_color, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Floating binary digits in between
        digits = VGroup()
        binary_pattern = ["1", "0", "1", "1", "0", "1"]
        for idx, bit in enumerate(binary_pattern):
            d_tex = Text(bit, font_size=32, color=WHITE)
            # Use column indices 1 through 6 in Row C
            self.place_at_grid(d_tex, f"C{idx+1}")
            digits.add(d_tex)
        
        bridge_group = VGroup(top_line, bottom_line, digits)
        
        self.play(Create(top_line), Create(bottom_line), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(digits, lag_ratio=0.15, shift=UP*0.2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(tower_highlight)
        
        # Formula '2^n - 1' on the left side of the bridge area
        formula = MathTex("2^n - 1", color=WHITE, font_size=48)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "D2")
        
        # 3-disk Tower of Hanoi stack on the right side of the bridge area
        # Define internal structure relative to its own center, then place group
        t_base = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        t_peg = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*1.0, color=WHITE)
        d3 = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.2, color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.1)
        d2 = Rectangle(width=0.9, height=0.2, color="#FFA500", fill_opacity=1).next_to(d3, UP, buff=0.05)
        d1 = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.2, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1).next_to(d2, UP, buff=0.05)
        tower = VGroup(t_base, t_peg, d3, d2, d1)
        # Position the whole tower in the right side area
        self.place_in_area(tower, "B5", "E6")
        
        self.play(
            Write(formula),
            FadeIn(tower, shift=RIGHT),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Update lecture line colors
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(final_white)
        
        # Group bridge, formula, and tower
        bridge_and_logic = VGroup(bridge_group, formula, tower)
        
        # Fade in the final 'Mathematical Elegance' title in the center of the grid area
        final_conclusion_title = Text("Mathematical Elegance", color=final_white, font_size=44)
        self.place_in_area(final_conclusion_title, "A1", "F6")
        
        self.play(
            bridge_and_logic.animate.scale(0.5).set_opacity(0.2),
            FadeIn(final_conclusion_title, scale=1.1),
            run_time=2.5
        )
        self.wait(5)

outline.topic: The Binary Secret of the Towers of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: High school students and introductory Computer Science students

sections.title: The Legend and the Rules
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle through the 'Legend of Brahma'. A character (a monk) must move 64 golden disks between three needles. Rules: 1. Move only one disk at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on a smaller one. State the goal: How can we find the perfect sequence of moves without getting lost?
sections.example: Visualizing a monk at an ancient temple with three stone pillars and 3 colorful disks to start.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Binary Counter
sections.content: Explain binary counting (base-2) using a visual 3-bit flip-counter. Show how numbers increment from 000 to 111. Emphasize the 'rightmost bit' (the least significant bit) and how it toggles every step, while the second bit toggles every two steps, and so on.
sections.example: A series of 3 light bulbs where 'On' is 1 and 'Off' is 0, counting from 0 (off-off-off) to 7 (on-on-on).

sections.title: The Mapping: Disks as Bits
sections.content: Establish the connection: The total number of moves for $n$ disks is $2^n - 1$. Map each disk to a bit position in a binary number. Disk 1 (smallest) corresponds to the 1st bit (2^0), Disk 2 to the 2nd bit (2^1), and so on. The 'Move Number' in binary tells us exactly which disk to touch.
sections.example: A graphic showing 3 disks stacked, with Disk 1 labeled 'Bit 0', Disk 2 'Bit 1', and Disk 3 'Bit 2'.

sections.title: The Rule of the Rightmost Set Bit
sections.content: Introduce the 'Magic Rule': To know which disk to move at any step $k$, look at the binary representation of $k$. The position of the 'rightmost 1' (the lowest set bit) identifies the disk. If the rightmost 1 is at the first position, move Disk 1. If it's at the second, move Disk 2.
sections.example: Step 4 in binary is '100'. The rightmost '1' is in the 3rd position. Therefore, at Step 4, you move Disk 3.

sections.title: Animated Walkthrough: 3-Disk Demo
sections.content: Sync a binary counter with the puzzle moves. Show the counter incrementing and the corresponding disk moving. Step 1 (001): Move Disk 1. Step 2 (010): Move Disk 2. Step 3 (011): Move Disk 1. Step 4 (100): Move Disk 3. Explain that Disk 1 always moves in a consistent cycle (A->B->C), while others follow based on availability.
sections.example: A split-screen animation: Left side shows a digital counter incrementing; Right side shows the physical disks jumping between pegs in real-time.

sections.title: Conclusion: Mathematical Elegance
sections.content: Summarize how binary counting transforms a complex recursive problem into a simple linear sequence. Highlight that this connection is why computers (which think in binary) are so efficient at solving recursive structures.
sections.example: A final graphic showing the 'Binary Bridge' connecting the world of numbers to the world of physical logic puzzles.
